epithet: Has the news of the Overwhelming reached you?
lede: Two kinds of faces on one Day: worn out and cast down, or radiant and at rest. Between the two pictures the surah asks its hearers to look at four things they pass every day — and tells the Prophet ﷺ that his task is to remind, not to compel.

names.name: al-Ghāshiyah
names.note: One of the names of the Resurrection: that which covers everything and everyone with its terrors. This is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said it is the Fire, which covers the faces of the disbelievers. The Prophet ﷺ called the surah by its opening, Hal atāka ḥadīthu l-ghāshiyah.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: both Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī record the agreement. The traditional order places it sixty-eighth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الغاشِيَةِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَهِيَ سِتٌّ وَعِشْرُونَ آيَةً

setting: No occasion is reported for it. It was, with al-Aʿlā, the surah the people of Madinah heard from the Prophet ﷺ more than any other in the great public prayers — every Friday, and at both ʿĪds — and so it is one of the passages by which the community has been reminded of the next life, week after week, since his time.

Its argument is made for people of the desert, and made with what the desert holds. Do they not look at the camel — how it was created? It was the Arab’s wealth, his transport, his food and drink, an animal that kneels to be loaded and carries a man across country that would kill him. And the sky, how it was raised; the mountains, how they were set; the earth, how it was spread out. A rider crossing the open land sees exactly those four things and nothing else.

Then comes one of the clearest statements in the Qurʾan of what a messenger is and is not. So remind: you are only one who reminds. You are not set over them as a controller. Their return is to Us, and their reckoning is Ours to take.
aim: To remind souls of the scenes of divine power in punishment and in bliss, and of its proofs in the signs before them — so that they are filled with longing and with awe.
themes: The faces of the Last Day
The Prophet ﷺ as a reminder

outline.title: Faces cast down
outline.summary: Has the news of the Overwhelming reached you? Faces that Day will be humbled, toiling and worn out, entering a scorching fire, given to drink from a boiling spring, with no food but a bitter thorn that neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.

outline.title: Faces at ease
outline.summary: Faces that Day will be joyful, well pleased with their striving, in a lofty garden where they hear no idle word: a flowing spring, couches raised high, cups set ready, cushions in rows and carpets spread.

outline.title: Four things to look at
outline.summary: Do they not look at the camels, how they were created; at the sky, how it was raised; at the mountains, how they were set up; and at the earth, how it was spread out?

outline.title: Only a reminder
outline.summary: So remind — you are only one who reminds; you are not a controller over them. But whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment. To Us is their return; then upon Us is their reckoning.

keyAyah.why: The Prophet’s ﷺ task, and the task of everyone who has passed on his message since, in two short ayat.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, in the two ʿĪds and on Friday, “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” and “Has the news of the Overwhelming reached you?” And when an ʿĪd and a Friday fell on the same day, he would recite them in both prayers.

before: Al-Aʿlā ended by saying the Hereafter is better and more lasting, and that the wretched will enter the greatest Fire. Al-Ghāshiyah shows both.
after: This surah speaks of faces humbled and toiling. Al-Fajr tells of peoples who toiled at power in this world — ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh — and what their Lord did with them.

notable.label: Do they not look at the camels?
